Photos to PDF

How to turn photos into a single PDF on iPhone

PaperVault · November 12, 2026 · 4 min read

To put several iPhone photos into one PDF, select only the images you need, arrange them in reading order, create the PDF, and review each page before sharing. A quick check catches sideways, duplicate, or hard-to-read photos.

Choose and prepare your photos

Select the clearest image of each page. If you are photographing paper, use even light, keep the page flat, and include all its edges. Avoid a photo with glare, motion blur, or another page visible underneath. For a document with multiple sheets, decide the order before converting them.

Convert the images into one PDF

  1. Open a PDF app and choose its image-to-PDF feature. PaperVault lists Images to PDF for selecting images.
  2. Select the photos and check the selection count. Remove screenshots or personal pictures that are not part of the document.
  3. Reorder the images so the PDF reads from its first page to its last. The App Store listing says PaperVault lets you reorder selected photos.
  4. Create the PDF and give the file a clear name.
  5. Open the finished PDF and check every page's orientation, crop, readability, and order.

Improve the result before sharing

Retake a page if text is blurry instead of hoping a PDF converter can restore detail that is not in the original image. Crop out unrelated surroundings without cutting off content. Keep page orientation consistent where possible. If the file is too large, make a compressed copy and inspect it before sending; do not delete the original photos until you know you have the pages you need.

Keep personal information in mind

Photos can include details beyond the document itself, such as a desk, another paper, or a person in the background. Review the edges of each image and each page of the created PDF. If you choose photos through an iOS system picker, review the picker and file provider you are using.

PaperVault note: The App Store listing describes turning selected, reordered photos into a PDF and processing PDF tools on-device.
